page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6a.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at 2.6 GHz. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. The instance exhibits poor single-core CPU performance and weak multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth is also weak, measuring 30.8 GB/sec for read operations and 15.87 GB/sec for write operations. However, cached small-block memory bandwidth remains average at 400.15 GB/sec. General processing capabilities, such as single-threaded gzip compression and PassMark CPU metrics, fall within the average range.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r6a.2xlarge offers a high density of memory relative to its processing cores, making it suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require extreme CPU throughput. Average performance in PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations (7.13 million operations per second) indicates suitability for caching layers, in-memory databases, and moderate web serving. It is less suited for compute-heavy tasks or applications requiring high local storage IOPS.
